maria_support: FYI — enterprise tenant T-723 submitted an erase request 2026-03-14 09:12 UTC for all embeddings for user_id u-402. They say queries still return vectors referencing that user and asked for audit proof/chain of deletion. They attached a short repro (see below).

maria_support: Customer reported two things: 1) embeddings search returns results for the erased user, 2) one of their engineers saw a 401 when calling our /v1/internal/kms/keys endpoint earlier today. Asking for exact evidence bundle for DPA: audit logs, KMS/HSM events, subprocessor chain. Can someone triage? :warning:

maria_support: Copied from customer (redacted):
```\n# Repro steps from customer\n# 1) Create embedding\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"tenant":"T-723","input":"private PII text for user u-402"}'\n# 2) Verify exists via vector search\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/search \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -d '{"tenant":"T-723","query":"u-402","k":5}'\n# 3) Customer submitted erase request via console UI at 2026-03-14T09:12:05Z (says UI returned job_id: job-5589)\n# 4) At 2026-03-16T08:41:12Z, embeddings search still returned the vector for that content (returned id 'vec-21')\n# 5) At 2026-03-16T08:44:01Z, engineer called internal kms endpoint and got HTTP/1.1 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}\n```\n
maria_support: Customer included a screenshot of job-5589 status: "Completed" in UI. They want definitive proof the underlying ciphertext/key material was destroyed or reference removed from search index and timestamps for when that happened.

ark_sre: Ack — will start by tracing the erase job job-5589. Quick notes: erase flows are two-stage for embeddings: 1) indexing layer tombstones vectors (fast), 2) downstream cold storage + backups + KMS/HSM key usage (async). Propagation to all read replicas can take up to 48h in worst-case, but we should confirm specific events for this tenant.

ark_sre: Commands I'll run (on-call):
- Search ML index logs: `kubectl logs -l app=vector-index -n redwood | grep job-5589`
- Check erase worker: `kubectl logs -l app=erase-worker -n redwood | grep "job-5589"`
- KMS request audit: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=kms-key-T-723` (or our internal KMS proxy logs)

dan_engineer: I'll repro locally in staging using the customer's steps. If staging returns still-present vectors after mark-complete, we can debug the tombstone-to-compact path. My suggested repro to run (internal):
```\n# reproduce (internal/staging)\nexport REDWOOD_KEY="stg-REDACTED"\n# create embedding\ncurl -s -X POST https://stg.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"tenant":"T-723","input":"test user u-402"}' | jq .id\n# submit erase\ncurl -s -X POST https://stg.api.redwood.ai/v1/erase -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"tenant":"T-723","job_name":"test-erase-u402","selector":{"user_id":"u-402"}}' | jq .job_id\n# poll job\ncurl -s https://stg.api.redwood.ai/v1/erase/job/job-XXXX -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"\n```\n
dan_engineer: If you still see vectors after job completes in staging, add a full dump of `vector-index` segment metadata: `curl http://vector-index-internal:9100/segments?tenant=T-723` and paste the JSON.

oliver_security: Add security checklist: we need the following items for the DPA evidence pack:
- erase job ID + timestamps (submitted, started, finished)
- vector index tombstone events with segment ids and timestamps
- KMS/HSM audit events showing Delete/Disable operations or key rotation fingerprints tied to the key used to encrypt tenant T-723 data
- list of subprocessor IDs involved in storage (S3-like object store, backup cluster, HSM vendor) and timestamps when each subprocessor acknowledged deletion
- confirmation of any retention policy (e.g., backups retention window) and whether a legal hold existed

oliver_security: For the 401 on the internal KMS endpoint, that usually indicates a short-lived credential rotated or a proxy auth failure. We should fetch the proxy logs (ark_sre above) and the KMS-proxy error lines. Also capture the `encryption_key_fingerprint` value so legal can tie it to a key rotation event.

sre-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-3457 - "T-723 erase evidence request". Assigned: ark_sre, dan_engineer, oliver_security. SLA: internal 72h evidence bundle.

ark_sre: Quick trace results (pulled logs, redacted):
```\n2026-03-14T09:12:07Z erase-worker[pid=412] INFO job=job-5589 tenant=T-723 selector={user_id:u-402} status=queued\n2026-03-14T09:12:12Z erase-worker[pid=412] INFO job=job-5589 tenant=T-723 status=in_progress\n2026-03-14T09:12:19Z vector-index[seg=7a2] INFO tombstone added segment=7a2 vect_count=1 selector=user_id:u-402\n2026-03-14T09:12:22Z erase-worker[pid=412] INFO job=job-5589 status=completed\n2026-03-16T08:44:01Z kms-proxy[pid=88] WARN request_id=req-3f2 tenant=T-723 path=/internal/kms/keys auth=failed status=401\n```\n
ark_sre: From these, tombstone was added and job marked completed. The remaining symptom likely due to stale search replicas or a failure in the background compaction that prunes tombstoned vectors from segments. I'll run a compaction snapshot for tenant T-723 and force reindex of affected segments. Will also collect KMS proxy logs around req-3f2 for the 401.

dan_engineer: I ran the staging repro. When I force-complete an erase job, the search result disappears from headless index but can still be served from cached replica for up to ~36h if compaction didn't run. I triggered `index-compact --tenant T-723 --segment 7a2` and that removed the vector.

dan_engineer: Suggest we tell the customer: their job-5589 completed, tombstone written 2026-03-14T09:12:19Z, compaction ran on 2026-03-16T09:05:10Z (I will schedule compaction now), and full propagation finished at 2026-03-16T09:16:02Z. Provide them the logs and segment ids.

oliver_security: Good. For the audit pack, I'll need: the compaction job id, the KMS request ids (both for reads and for key operations), and the HSM vendor acknowledgement (if HSM is used for that tenant). Ark, can you export cloudtrail/cloud-logging events for resource `kms-key-T-723` between 2026-03-13 and 2026-03-17 and drop them into the evidence S3 bucket with access policy for legal?

ark_sre: On it — exporting now to s3://redwood-evidence/INC-2026-3457/T-723/ (will grant oliver_security + legal_read). Note: there is an internal retention policy that keeps backups for 30 days; if customer requested destruction of backups, we need to confirm whether a backup snapshot was taken prior to erase and whether retention policy allows immediate purge or only scheduled deletion.

maria_support: Draft reply to customer for immediate response: "Thanks, we received your erase request and job-5589 completed. Tombstone and index removal were initiated 2026-03-14; compaction and full propagation completed 2026-03-16 at ~09:16 UTC. We're assembling the audit pack (index tombstone logs, compaction log, KMS/HSM audit events and subprocessor acknowledgements) and will deliver within 72 hours. If you require a faster SLA we can escalate." Thoughts? :+1:

dan_engineer: LGTM. Add the small repro & commands we used as an appendix so they can see steps we ran. Omit internal hostnames and any broad log dumps; give per-item log excerpts and signed checksums (sha256) of the evidence bundle.

oliver_security: Also include: confirmation whether the tenant used our managed KMS or a customer-managed key (CMK). If CMK, we must ask the customer to confirm deletion on their KMS side — we can't destroy keys in a customer-owned KMS.

maria_support: Thanks all — I'll send the customer the timeline + commit to the evidence link once ark uploads. Marking thread for follow-up after evidence upload. :white_check_mark:
